newsitem.title: ESTONIA: THOMSON SAY MAY RAISE LATVIA, LITHUANIA RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: THOMSON SAY MAY RAISE LATVIA, LITHUANIA RATINGS.

text.p: Thomson Bankwatch said on Thursday that it may raise its BB- sovereign ratings on Latvia and Lithuania.

Thomson Bankwatch-BRE president Ramin Habibi told Reuters that the ratings would be reconsidered after the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) meeting in London and after further visits to Latvia and Lithuania.
"I expect one or both (ratings) to be raised," Habibi said in an interview.
The rating for Lithuania was last done in October 1996 while Latvia's was carried out in January.
Habibi said his company hoped to keep increasing its coverage of the Baltic states and said there was steady international interest.
"I dont think there has been an increase, there has been a steady demand for them (Baltic ratings), he said.
"There has been a demand locally and also among clients in northern Europe," he said.
Thomson yesterday announced that it rated Estonia as BBB-, the first rating that Estonia has gained.
